output.content:
Arm’s Neoverse franchise is the CPU/IP layer behind a growing portion of hyperscaler and AI-data-center compute: Arm reported that Neoverse has surpassed 1 billion deployed cores and that it expected its share of CPU compute at top hyperscalers to approach 50%. [[1]] 

AWS is the clearest custom-silicon example: its Graviton family is designed for Amazon EC2, and the latest Graviton5 is built on Arm Neoverse CSS V3 with 192 cores—double Graviton4’s core count. [[2]] [[1]] 

NVIDIA is the AI-system example: each Grace CPU contains 72 Arm Neoverse V2 cores, while the dual-chip Grace CPU Superchip contains 144 cores connected through NVLink-C2C. [[3]] 

Grace Blackwell combines this Arm-based Grace CPU platform with NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs; for example, NVIDIA’s GB200 NVL4 uses two Grace CPUs linked over NVLink-C2C with four Blackwell GPUs. [[4]] 

The investment implication is that Arm participates in both general-purpose cloud CPU displacement of x86—via products such as AWS Graviton, Google Axion, and Microsoft Cobalt—and in AI infrastructure, where Grace/Blackwell places Arm CPU compute alongside GPU accelerators. [[5]] [[6]] 

The important qualification is that the “nearly 50%” hyperscaler figure is Arm management’s expectation, rather than an independently measured industry shipment-share statistic. [[5]] [[1]]
